summary: Shirasaka Mugi, in his final summer of high school, plans to move to the city and confess to his longtime first love, Kashii, who moved away abruptly four years earlier. Before Mugi can seek him out, Kashii unexpectedly returns to visit his grandfather, and Mugi persuades him to come to his family's bakery. There, Kashii reunites with Mugi's older brother, Daichi, who used to tutor him and now teaches science at a middle school. Mugi struggles to confess his feelings and instead reveals that he will enter beauty school in the city next April, asking whether they can meet regularly. Kashii warmly agrees and also accepts Mugi's request to stay at his home during the current summer vacation, ending the chapter with them arranging a visit.

Kashii declines a classmate’s invitation to meet Mugi, a hometown friend four years younger whom he regards as a little brother. Mugi arrives with newly dyed silver hair, and Kashii protects him from a street scam before leading him home while holding his hand. At Kashii’s apartment, Mugi is touched to find his favorite latte waiting and admits how lonely he has felt since Kashii moved away. Mugi confesses that he has loved Kashii romantically since childhood, but Kashii hesitates and apologizes. Knowing about Kashii’s feelings for his older brother, Daichi, Mugi asks whether Kashii still loves Daichi and whether Mugi could be the one by his side, leaving the answer unresolved.

Mugi insists that his longtime love for Mao is serious, and Mao, who says he has moved on from Daichi, eventually agrees to date him and take his feelings seriously. Mugi is thrilled but becomes flustered by their new intimacy, even though they have always been physically close. On a seaside date, Mugi recalls Mao’s beauty in their childhood and promises to stay beside him when he feels lonely or troubled. Mao initially kisses Mugi’s forehead, but they then share Mugi’s first kiss, leaving him overwhelmed. Back home, Mao teases Mugi about his sexual thoughts, and the chapter ends with Mao privately admitting that he had only intended a forehead kiss and that his own reactions are exceeding his expectations.

Mao rushes home after Mugi tells him his grandfather has been hospitalized, but is relieved to discover that he has only strained his back. Mugi reflects that Mao's fisherman father died at sea and his grandfather raised him, explaining why Mao was so frightened. Back at Mao's family home, Mugi cooks his favorite croquettes, and they enjoy an affectionate evening together before eating watermelon on the veranda. Mao decides to stay overnight, draws Mugi close, and asks permission to kiss him again, leading to increasingly intimate contact. Mao eventually stops and reassures Mugi, who is left confused by his own sense of relief.

Mugi and Mao enjoy a hometown date at an arcade before Mao’s former classmates draw them into a karaoke reunion. Mugi learns that Mao stopped fighting and became more outwardly sociable around the time Mugi’s older brother left home, though his friendly smile now seems emotionally distant. When the others try to pair Mao with Miu, he says he is already dating someone, delighting Mugi, and then slips away to spend time alone with him. Their kisses lead to a discussion about greater intimacy, but Mao refuses to continue because he fears hurting Mugi and doubts whether Mugi’s love will last. Hurt by Mao dismissing his feelings and deciding their limits alone, Mugi remains certain of his love and ends the chapter by asking what Mao himself is afraid of.
